title: 14th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting ran from 10:32 to 11:51 and opened with 32 members present. Members continued debating the government's bill to amend the Tourism Act (Law 2/99), sponsored by the Thimarafushi member, with supporters saying it would let long-closed resorts reopen and critics objecting to the powers, rent discounts and trust fund it adds; the debate was punctuated by points of order and exchanges over the opposition's urgent motions. After the sponsor's closing remarks the bill was accepted for consideration 43 to 9 and sent to the Economic Committee. The Majlis then approved three non-resident ambassador appointments (Philippines, Spain, New Zealand) with no debate, each with 54 votes in favour.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the amendment and said it passes powers held by the President under the decentralisation law to island councils.
Said the opposition's urgent motions often prove baseless, citing a 2020 case, and urged members to pass improvements to bills.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the Tourism Act amendment would ease council land leasing and restart resort projects, backing a time limit on closures.
Said tourist arrivals are up 4.9% on last year and described current borrowing and repayments as mainly dealing with debt inherited from earlier governments.
Presented Foreign Relations Committee reports finding the three nominated non-resident ambassadors qualified.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Said the amendments mostly put existing practice into law and urged quick passage; criticised the MDP's past handling of tourism investment.
Raised a point of order that remarks off the bill were not relevant; the Chair did not accept it as a point of order.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order that a member's remarks were not about a bill before the Majlis; the Chair did not accept it.
Said the changes move island and lagoon powers to the President and urged resort operators to wait for a larger discount.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said the government is not running the country and the Majlis has little real work; argued members should address Ramadan food prices instead.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Backed the amendment; said resort leases on council-area land have stalled, and the change would restart projects and open jobs for island youth.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Raised a point of order that a remark was being pinned on the wrong Galolhu member; the Chair asked members to name constituencies correctly.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Noted this is the third Tourism Act amendment in about eight months and questioned the rent-discount changes.
Warned the proposed trust fund could let money be spent without budget approval and criticised the government's handling of finances.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said provisions letting the government take back resorts closed for repairs may conflict with the Constitution's protection of property.
Warned new advertising, signboard and annual compliance-report rules would add costs and burdens for resorts.
Said the Majlis needs a clear rule for urgent motions, citing a refused motion on reported government money printing.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Said making and amending laws is the Majlis's core duty and the amendment would let long-closed resorts reopen, citing a closed resort in Addu City.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Agreed with the previous speaker; said closed resorts in Addu City such as Shangri-La cost local jobs, and called the amendment important.
Said the state should also receive tax, rent and income from resorts.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the amendment, noting the Tourism Act has been amended about 26 times in 26 years, many under MDP governments.
Said about 170 leased resort islands remain undeveloped, including some in his constituency, and the bill offers a route to develop them.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: As the bill's sponsor, thanked members for the debate and said the amendments would help reopen idle resorts and benefit island communities.

decisions: Debate on the Tourism Act (Law 2/99) amendment bill closed after the sponsor's reply.
The Tourism Act amendment bill was accepted for consideration and sent to the Economic Committee.
Dr Mariyam Shabeena Ahmed approved as non-resident ambassador to the Philippines.
Irushaam Adam approved as non-resident ambassador to Spain.
Mohamed Luveyz approved as non-resident ambassador to New Zealand.
Next sitting set for Thursday 13 March 2025 at 10:30.
